title: model-variant-failure-modes-postmortem-arch-sync
purpose: Postmortem and architecture sync after 2025-11-12 incident where routing fallbacks and cross-variant KV cache behavior caused p95 latency spikes and higher token cost for Dedicated customers.
context_summary: Traffic surge on Dedicated pool triggered cascading fallbacks (primary -> quantized -> smaller arch) which caused KV cache misses, repeated warmups, batch inefficiencies and a ~2.3x p95 latency increase for ~45 minutes. Incident tracked INF-8421.
agenda: Owners, next steps, RFCs to write
timeline_highlights: 11:03 - autoscaler slower due to pod eviction/placement oscillation (SRE)
11:07 - routing started cascading fallbacks: original -> quantized -> smaller-arch -> cached-prefix
11:08-11:25 - repeated KV cache misses and warmups, increased cache churn and memory pressure
11:48 - stabilization after capacity ramp and manual scaling
root_cause_breakdown: Routing policy lacked hysteresis and per-session affinity, enabling churn when primary nodes returned
KV cache keys differ across quantized/arch variants causing misses even for same app-level prompt prefixes
High sequence-length variance prevented efficient batching during bursts
Autoscaler reaction slower than needed causing a capacity hole
Alerts were not sensitive to cross-variant cache-miss ratios or p95 token-work
impact_summary: Affected Dedicated customers in us-west-2 with hybrid routing enabled
~45 minutes of elevated p95 latency and higher token/GPU minutes
Customer visible increased latency and some 503s on long conversations
Internal cost: extra GPU minutes and model artifact transfers
short_term_mitigations: M1 (deployed 11:25): disable cross-region fallbacks for Dedicated pools
M2 (deployed 11:40): add per-session affinity (sticky routing) TTL=5m for Dedicated
M3 (in testing): KV cache write-through on first fallback (PR serving-runtime#1293)
Observability: add dashboards for cross-variant cache-miss rate and fallback chain length
discussion_long_term_options: Option A: Canonical prefix key mapping at router boundary so variants share KV entries (favored)
Option B: Hysteresis + session stickiness window (1-15m configurable) as low-risk measure
Option C: Keep warm-up replicas per variant and speculative KV population (higher cost/complexity)
Option D: Rework fallback ordering to include SLO and token-cost estimates via Optimize integration
decision: Short-term: implement Option B (hysteresis + session stickiness) default 5m Dedicated / 2m Hosted. Medium-term: RFC for Option A (canonical prefix mapping) with security and model-ops review. Long-term: evaluate Option D; deprioritize Option C.
design_notes_constraints: Canonical key proposal: canonical_prefix_hash = salted SHA256(prefix) suggested; avoid including model_artifact_version to allow sharing across variants, but discuss collision tradeoffs
Security: salted hash management via control-plane KMS and security sign-off required
Migration: read-through fallback to canonical key before switching to canonical-first under feature flag
Metrics to capture: cross-variant cache-hit ratio, fallback chain length histogram, KV write amplification
action_items: Evan: draft RFC for Canonical Prefix Mapping and migration plan. Target RFC-2026-11 by 2025-12-05 (INF-8490)
Priya: implement session-hysteresis config, add tests, canary rollout by 2025-11-26
Samir: spike KV read-through shim and perf numbers by 2025-11-28
Olivia: create dashboards + alerts for cross-variant cache-miss rate and fallback chain length by 2025-11-21
Diego: enumerate quantized variant key differences and update model onboarding checklist by 2025-11-24
Asha: draft customer comms for Dedicated customers first draft by 2025-11-21
open_questions: Should canonical key include model-id to avoid accidental cross-model collisions?
What TTLs should canonical keys use and how to avoid stale caches after model updates?
What is the privacy review path for salted prefix hashes and does current KMS posture suffice?
appendix: Temporary mitigation PR: serving-runtime#1293 toggles cross-region fallback and adds stickiness TTL config
Related tickets: INF-8421 (incident), INF-8490 (RFC), INF-8522 (observability), INF-8560 (model-ops checklist)
notes_to_self: Follow RFC sync with security and model-ops before implementation. Re-run perf scenario with synthetic bursts using customer X seq-dist once hysteresis is canaried.
raw_meeting_chatter: We saw variant churn cause repeated KV writes - that's the real cost driver, not model size alone. - Samir
If the canonical key is too generic we might hit privacy red flags. Security needs to sign off before rollout. - Olivia
Hysteresis buys us time; canonical mapping gives us the durable fix. - Diego
status_note: Working postmortem; tracking actions via INF tickets. Expect RFC and timeline updates in next weekly arch sync.
